"
Photosynthesis: balance
1 · Per CO₂ fixed
"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eDe los 6 G3P, \u003cb:
"

Of the 6 G3P, only 1 leaves the cycle (used to synthesize glucose, sucrose or starch); the other 5 G3P (15 C) are rearranged to regenerate 3 RuBP (15 C) with 3 ATP. Balance per CO₂ fixed: 3 ATP + 2 NADPH. For one glucose (6 CO₂): 18 ATP + 12 NADPH. In this way the energy of light is stored in C–H and C–C bonds.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEn el estroma, la \u0:
"

In the stroma, RuBisCO joins CO₂ to ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate (RuBP, 5 C) and the 6 C intermediate splits into 2 × 3-phosphoglycerate (3-PGA, 3 C). Then, 3-PGA is phosphorylated with ATP and reduced with NADPH to glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate (G3P). For 3 CO₂ fixed: 3 RuBP + 3 CO₂ → 6 PGA → 6 G3P (6 ATP + 6 NADPH).

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa fotosíntesis ocurr:
"

Photosynthesis takes place in the chloroplast, surrounded by two membranes. Inside, the stroma (fluid) contains the thylakoids, flattened sacs stacked in grana; the interior space of each thylakoid is the lumen. The light reactions (light-dependent) occur in the thylakoid membrane; the Calvin cycle (CO₂ fixation), in the stroma. Overall equation: 6 CO₂ + 12 H₂O + light → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6 O₂ + 6 H₂O.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLos \u003cb\u003epigm:
"

The pigments (chlorophylls a and b, carotenoids) capture photons, mainly in the blue (≈ 430–450 nm) and red (≈ 660–680 nm), and transfer the energy to the reaction center of photosystem II (P680). When excited, P680 gives up an electron; to replace it, the oxygen-evolving complex splits water: 2 H₂O → 4 H⁺ + 4 e⁻ + O₂. The O₂ released comes from water, not from CO₂, and the H⁺ remain in the lumen.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLos electrones pasan:
"

The electrons pass through the transport chain: PSII → plastoquinone (PQ) → cytochrome b₆f complex → plastocyanin (PC) → PSI. At b₆f the energy released pumps H⁺ from the stroma into the lumen. Together with photolysis, this creates a proton gradient (the lumen reaches pH ≈ 4–5; the stroma ≈ 8): a proton-motive force. A second photon excites PSI (P700) and sends the electron to an even higher energy level (Z scheme).

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLos H⁺ vuelven al est:
"

The H⁺ return to the stroma through ATP synthase: the flow turns its rotor and catalyzes ADP + Pᵢ → ATP (photophosphorylation, about 4 H⁺ per ATP). In PSI, the electrons, through ferredoxin and FNR, reduce NADP⁺ + H⁺ + 2 e⁻ → NADPH. The product of the light phase is ATP + NADPH + O₂; with intense light the carriers saturate.

"
